defects.shape: <video> whose OWN assetRef is a dangling id (not present in the asset catalog) while its media arrives from resolvable <source> children.
defects.measured: tmp/wr285b/reverify-video/truthtable.ts case b2 -> unresolvedElementAssets = 1 at the parent, although the element renders its child's media correctly.
defects.why: The GAP-B early return requires assets.length > 0, so refs that resolve to nothing keep falling through to noSrcAtAll -> unresolved, and compile-node's <source>-child guard is keyed on noOwnMediaAsset, which that path never sets. This is the same asymmetry class GAP-B removed, surviving for dangling refs.
defects.correctionAwareness: Explicitly documented and chosen in asset-resolver.ts's GAP-B comment ('refs that resolve to nothing at all have no kind to inspect and remain a genuine catalog failure'). Defensible — a dangling ref IS a real SiteSpec/catalog defect — but the increment is attributed to the video's media rather than to the catalog.

defects.shape: A <video> with N <source> children that ALL have zero assetRefs counts N, not 1.
defects.measured: truthtable case e2 -> 2 broken <source> children, unresolvedElementAssets = 2, parent 0.
defects.judgment: Consistent with the correction's stated invariant (one increment per ELEMENT whose media is lost) and with how has always been counted; the alternative (collapse to 1) would need cross-element bookkeeping. Recorded so a future reader does not read unresolvedElementAssets as 'number of broken media surfaces'.
